TL;DR

Company: Sensei Labs
Product: Conductor — the AI-powered operating system for strategic programs
Reports to: CTO
Team: 7 direct reports (4 software engineers, 2 quality engineers, and the Platform/DevOps team)
Partnering closely: 2-person Product team and 4-person GTM team
Location: [Toronto / remote]

About Us

Sensei Labs builds Conductor, an enterprise strategy execution platform that governs billions of dollars in program value across hundreds of enterprise programs. Our customers are Fortune 500 transformation offices, global consultancies, and private equity value creation teams. Conductor covers the full lifecycle from portfolio planning through benefits realization, with our Harmony AI layer woven into every surface rather than bolted on.

We've been in the market for more than ten years, we're SOC-2 compliant with a single-tenant architecture, and we do all of it with a deliberately small team. That's the interesting part of this job.

We launched a full rewrite of our Conductor platform a few months ago and are midway through the effort to reach Conductor Modern. Over the next year (or so), this will give us the chance to migrate all our customers and partners to the new version and sunset our old code.

The role

You'll own engineering execution for Conductor: how the team is structured, how work gets from idea to production, and how quickly and reliably we ship. You'll drive the technical strategy and architecture direction, and you'll own the machine that turns that direction into shipped software.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a role that manages managers. With six engineers, you'll be in the code, in the reviews, and in the architecture discussions — while also being the person accountable for delivery, hiring, growth, and the team's day-to-day health. If you want a position where you can both set long-term strategy and have immediate day-to-day impact, this is the seat.

As part of our modernization, you’ll be directly involved in any remaining architectural and technical decisions for Conductor Modern and be a key part of planning for the customer migration and the ultimate sunsetting of the existing codebase.

This is the third leg of the Sensei Labs stool, along with our established Product and GTM leaders. You’ll work closely with them to shape and implement Product’s vision and to enable our GTM team to sell and deliver value to our customers and partners.

What You'll Own

Delivery. Planning, sequencing, and shipping against a roadmap you help build with Product. Predictable releases, visible progress, honest tradeoffs.
The team. Coaching and growing six engineers, running performance and career conversations, hiring as we scale, and keeping the bar high without burning people out.
Cloud platform and reliability. Architecture, scalability, cost, and operational excellence for a single-tenant enterprise SaaS platform. Uptime, performance, and security posture are yours. You'll lead our Platform/DevOps team alongside product engineering, setting direction for infrastructure and application architecture, performance and scalability, cloud cost management, and the tooling that the rest of engineering builds on. Uptime, operational excellence, and security posture are yours.
AI in the product. Partnering with Product on how Harmony AI evolves — agentic workflows, retrieval, evaluation, guardrails, and permission-aware AI behavior in an enterprise context.
AI in how we build. Making our SDLC substantially faster and more automated: AI-assisted coding, code review, and test generation; CI/CD; automated quality gates. We want an engineering org where a small team ships like a large one, and you'll be the one who builds that.
Engineering–Product partnership. Working shoulder to shoulder with Product on discovery, scope, and sequencing. You'll be expected to have opinions about the product, not just the plumbing.
Enterprise trust. Security, compliance, and the technical side of customer and prospect conversations when it matters.

What We're Looking For

Cloud infrastructure and application architecture at depth.

You've architected, built, and operated production cloud SaaS at meaningful scale — not just supervised it. You're fluent across both layers: the application architecture (service boundaries, data modeling, API design, and the patterns that keep a large codebase evolvable) and the infrastructure underneath it. Hands-on depth in Azure and/or GCP is essential, along with container orchestration on Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, networking and identity, and the observability and cost discipline that keep a cloud platform healthy as it grows. You understand multi-tenancy versus single-tenancy tradeoffs, data isolation, performance under enterprise load, and what "SOC-2 compliant" actually costs an engineering team.

Real product instinct.

You've worked in product-led environments where engineering shapes what gets built. You can push back on a spec, spot the simpler solution, and reason about customer value — especially in complex B2B software where the user is an enterprise operator, not a consumer.

Team leadership with your hands still dirty.

You've led and grown engineering teams (roughly 5–20 people) as a player-coach. You've hired well, given hard feedback, and relentlessly tuned the delivery process.

AI fluency, both directions.

You've shipped AI or LLM-backed features into production — and you've also rebuilt how a team works using AI-assisted development and automated SDLC tooling. You can tell the difference between AI that creates leverage and AI that creates cleanup work.

Startup temperament.

You're comfortable being both the strategist and the person who fixes the flaky test. You'd rather own an outcome than a headcount number.

Nice to have

Enterprise PPM, EPMO, transformation, or professional services domain experience
Experience with Microsoft 365 / SAP / Jira / Power BI integration ecosystems
Background in selling or supporting technical evaluations with Fortune 500 or PE buyers
Experience taking a mature product through an AI-era re-platforming or modernization

Your first year

By 90 days — you know the codebase, the team, and the roadmap; you've shipped something meaningful yourself; and you've given us a clear read on our biggest delivery and technical risks.
By 6 months — the development lifecycle is measurably faster, with AI-assisted workflows and automated quality gates that the team actually uses. Release cadence is predictable.
By 12 months — engineering is a genuine competitive advantage: shipping AI capability into Conductor at a pace that surprises much larger competitors, with a team that's grown in both size and capability.

Why this role

Small team, real enterprise customers, an established product, and an unusually good excuse to rebuild how software gets made. You won't be one VP among many, and you won't be managing a slide deck about AI transformation — you'll be doing it, on a product whose entire premise is helping large organizations actually execute.

The Vice President of Strategy, Technology & Operations shapes how Great Bay Credit and Finance (GBCF) grows, operates, and scales. The role identifies high-value investment opportunities, leads the adoption of business-enhancing technologies, and oversees post-execution portfolio operations, including administration, surveillance, reporting, and controls for interconnection security financing transactions and related credit solutions.

Success requires strategic judgment, analytical rigor, strong organization, fluency with technology and data systems, and the ability to lead change. Working closely with GBCF leadership, the successful candidate will turn market insights and portfolio data into actionable strategy. This is not a software engineering role; it leads the evaluation, piloting, deployment, and adoption of technologies that improve portfolio management, workflow automation, reporting, data quality, and decision-making.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Shape GBCF’s growth strategy by identifying and evaluating new markets, products, counterparties, interconnection processes, and other high-value investment opportunities
Lead the selection, piloting, deployment, and adoption of technology and data systems that strengthen portfolio management, workflow automation, reporting, data quality, and decision-making
Own post-execution portfolio operations, including administration, surveillance, reporting, controls, deadlines, documentation, and counterparty coordination
Build scalable portfolio data, analytics, dashboards, and reporting capabilities that support management, capital-provider, and board decision-making
Lead cross-functional initiatives and translate market insight, portfolio information, and operating experience into actionable recommendations for GBCF leadership

STRATEGY

Perform strategic market research and analysis to identify new, high-value investment opportunities, including new markets, products, counterparty segments, and interconnection processes
Evaluate existing investment theses for opportunities and identify regulatory, market, counterparty, and structural risks
Use data and technology to identify portfolio optimization opportunities
Monitor regulatory, tariff, and market developments and their implications for GBCF’s strategy
Develop and present strategic recommendations, market assessments, and supporting analysis to GBCF leadership

TECHNOLOGY

 Lead the design and improvement of GBCF’s portfolio management systems.
Evaluate and recommend software, workflow, database, data-management, and AI tools.
Manage technology pilots, including success criteria, coordination, and results assessment.
Lead implementation, integration, migration, process redesign, training, documentation, and value tracking.
Automate manual processes, reduce operational risk, and centralize portfolio data and reporting.

OPERATIONS

Own recurring portfolio-management processes and controls following transaction execution
Oversee deposit calendars, milestone tracking, utility notices, invoice processing, covenant reporting, and letter-of-credit issuances, renewals, amendments, substitutions, and releases
Monitor obligations and deadlines across the portfolio and coordinate communications relating to deposits, letters of credit, milestones, notices, invoices, deadlines, and reporting requirements
Serve as a responsive point of contact for developers, utilities, ISOs, lenders, and other counterparties, and support counterparties through complex administrative and operational processes
Ensure accurate records and documentation are maintained

ANALYTICS & REPORTING

Ensure portfolio data integrity and reporting accuracy
Produce concentration, refundability, exposure, and portfolio-monitoring reports
Lead the design and launch of dashboards and automated reporting workflows
Support forecasting, capital-provider reporting, management reporting, and board reporting

QUALIFICATIONS

Significant professional experience, typically five or more years, in strategy, operations, technology, finance, or related roles, including experience leading cross-functional initiatives
Demonstrated ability to conduct strategic market research and translate analysis into actionable recommendations
Track record of evaluating, piloting, deploying, and driving organizational adoption of new technologies
Strong understanding of databases, data structures, and business systems, with working knowledge of APIs, system integrations, and workflow automation concepts
Experience creating dashboards, reports, and operational analytics
Strong project-management, change-management, and organizational skills
Advanced Excel proficiency and strong analytical capabilities
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present to senior leadership.

LOCATION

Full-time, in-office role based in Portsmouth, NH. Candidates may be located in the greater New England area, provided they are able to work from the Portsmouth office on a full-time basis.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Great Bay Renewables offers a competitive compensation and benefits package commensurate with the successful candidate’s experience, qualifications, and responsibilities
401(k) employer match; health, dental, and vision insurance starting day one; Flexible Paid Time Off and Holiday PTO; and cell phone reimbursement
Relocation bonus available

ABOUT GREAT BAY ROYALTIES

Great Bay Royalties, based in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, provides capital to the renewable energy sector in exchange for royalties in renewable energy generating facilities at all stages in their life cycle. To date, Great Bay has committed more than $1.2 billion in royalty financing into the energy sector royalties and interconnection support and has royalty agreements on nearly 9 GWs of projects expected to be operating or in construction by the end of 2026. Great Bay’s management team has extensive experience in renewable energy development, financing, and operations across a range of renewable technologies located throughout the United States. Great Bay is backed by Altius Renewable Royalties Corp. (TSX: ARR) (OTCQX: ATRWF) and certain funds managed by affiliates of Northampton Capital Partners.

ABOUT GREAT BAY CREDIT AND FINANCE

Great Bay Credit and Finance partners with energy infrastructure developers by providing innovative royalty investment capital and credit solutions that enable project development, growth, and the long-term success of energy infrastructure projects. GBCF is a division within Great Bay Renewables that provides credit solutions focused on generation and large-load interconnection security financing. GBCF seeks to create value through strong partnerships, disciplined execution, and innovative solutions that address evolving market needs.

You'll lead one of the most consequential parts of Stord's business at a moment when the company is growing fast and the stakes for getting Logistics right have never been higher.

LMS gives you a direct line from engineering work to bottom-line warehouse cost savings across the entire network, not just one site.

You'll inherit a strong bench (five managers and a Principal Engineer) and have real authority to shape how that org performs, not just maintain it.

Org & Talent Leadership

Own performance and accountability across five engineering managers and a Principal Engineer, setting a clear bar for what good looks like on each team.

Billing Automation

Partner directly with Finance leadership to drive the end-to-end automation of Stord's billing process.

Surface and resolve the cross-functional blockers that typically stall finance-engineering initiatives.

A track record of driving outcomes, not activity. You can point to specific business results (cost savings, revenue, delivery predictability) that your organizations produced under your leadership.

Strong Communication: You communicate clearly with engineers, PMs, and executives. You translate technical complexity into business language and vice versa.
